I’m Will Brooke. I work on greenhouse-gas reporting and verification as a regulator. That work often comes down to a practical question: what evidence would let someone outside the project judge what was claimed?

This site is where I ask a related question about AI agents. If I give an agent authority to do a job on someone else’s behalf, what do I need to establish before it acts? Afterward, what can the person affected find out about what happened, and if something doesn't go as planned, who can put it right?

The working note, [Assuring one delegation](notes/delegation-assurance/index.qmd), sets out the proposal, and the [Tests](cases/index.qmd) page summarizes the small experiments behind it.

Separately, I've made a small text game, [Off Script](off-script.qmd), about meeting strangers as equals: the everyday version of the same questions about standing and accountability.

I write here in a personal capacity. If you’ve run into a case that would put these ideas to the test, I’d like to hear about it: [will@emberwall.net](mailto:will@emberwall.net)
